title: Dower House residents enjoy close encounters with rescued birds of prey
excerpt: An afternoon of close encounters with birds of prey took flight at care home recently.
content:
Birds of prey visit Winchester care home residents

 

Residents with birds of prey. (Image: The Dower House)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

An afternoon of close encounters with birds of prey took flight at a care home recently.

The Dower House Care Home in Headbourne Worthy, Winchester, welcomed a visit from Colin of Bird of Prey and Owl Rescue, who introduced residents to a variety of owls and other raptors while sharing educational stories about their care and backgrounds.

The visit aimed to raise awareness of the rescue charity’s work in rehabilitating and rehoming sick, injured, or vulnerable birds of prey.

Christine Farmery, activities co-ordinator at The Dower House, said: "Visits like this are a wonderful example of the varied and meaningful activities we provide for our residents.

"We are always looking for opportunities to bring new experiences into the home, whether that's through animals, music, arts, community groups or educational talks.

"The birds sparked so many conversations and memories, and it was lovely to see residents so engaged and interested throughout the afternoon."

Residents expressed delight at the chance to meet the birds up close.

Mrs Karren, one of the residents, said: "I absolutely loved meeting the birds. They were so beautiful and majestic, and it was wonderful to be able to see them so close up."
